prompt:
Scene:
A top-down square photograph of an open sketch journal on a small round café table, morning sun slanting across from the upper right. A saucer with a half-drunk espresso sits just beside the right page casting a warm ring shadow. The journal has oat-colored paper and a linen-wrapped spine.

Subject:
A café observational diary spread. The left page has a quick ink drawing of two strangers reading books, surrounded by shorthand marks about light and clothing, and a pencil gesture drawing of the café counter. The right page contains a slow handwritten text block with occasional crossed-out lines, a taped-in coaster with a coffee ring on it, and a small palette swatch of ivory, espresso brown, rust, and butter yellow painted with a travel watercolor kit.

Important details:
The quick ink sketches must feel confident but unfinished — some lines break mid-stroke, some figures lose a leg. The coffee ring on the coaster must be a real stain edge. Crossed-out handwriting must show pen-pressure marks through to the back side as a faint ghost. The palette swatch carries physical pigment pooling. The warm ambient light must feel like morning café, not studio flash.

Use case:
Independent single image in the Scrapbook Variations package, representing the observational illustrator voice.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, no brand names, no over-finished sketches, no vector gesture lines, no flat gradient, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio.
title: Coffee Shop Afternoon
description: An observational sketch-journal spread with quick ink figures, a taped coffee-stained coaster, and a travel-kit watercolor swatch.
